claim: Context-dependent changes in genetic interactions are an important feature of cellular pathways and their varying responses under different environmental conditions.
source: Context-dependent changes in genetic interactions are an important feature of cellular pathways and their varying responses under different environmental conditions.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that establishes the importance of the research topic based on established scientific understanding.

claim: Methodological frameworks to investigate the plasticity of genetic interaction networks over time or in response to external stresses are largely lacking.
source: However, methodological frameworks to investigate the plasticity of genetic interaction networks over time or in response to external stresses are largely lacking.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current research methods, based on the authors' assessment of the field.

claim: The authors performed a combinatorial RNAi screen in Drosophila cells at multiple time points and after pharmacological inhibition of Ras signaling activity.
source: To analyze the plasticity of genetic interactions, we performed a combinatorial RNAi screen in Drosophila cells at multiple time points and after pharmacological inhibition of Ras signaling activity.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: The study assessed the effect of 12768 pairwise RNAi perturbations in six different conditions using an image-based morphology assay.
source: Using an image-based morphology assay to capture a broad range of phenotypes, we assessed the effect of 12768 pairwise RNAi perturbations in six different conditions.
evidence: This quantifies the scale of the experimental screen performed.

claim: Genetic interactions form in different trajectories.
source: We found that genetic interactions form in different trajectories and developed an algorithm, termed MODIFI, to analyze how genetic interactions rewire over time.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study based on the experimental data.

claim: The authors developed an algorithm termed MODIFI to analyze how genetic interactions rewire over time.
source: We found that genetic interactions form in different trajectories and developed an algorithm, termed MODIFI, to analyze how genetic interactions rewire over time.
evidence: This describes a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: MODIFI identified more statistically significant interactions compared to end-point assays.
source: Using this framework, we identified more statistically significant interactions compared to end-point assays and further observed several examples of context-dependent crosstalk between signaling pathways such as an interaction between Ras and Rel which is dependent on MEK activity.
evidence: This is a comparative finding demonstrating the advantage of the new method.

claim: There is context-dependent crosstalk between Ras and Rel signaling pathways that is dependent on MEK activity.
source: Using this framework, we identified more statistically significant interactions compared to end-point assays and further observed several examples of context-dependent crosstalk between signaling pathways such as an interaction between Ras and Rel which is dependent on MEK activity.
evidence: This is a specific biological finding from the study.

claim: Statistical genetic interactions are defined as an unexpected phenotypic outcome observed upon simultaneous perturbations of two genes that cannot be explained from the genes' individual effects.
source: In past studies, statistical genetic interactions (also simply referred to as genetic interactions) have been defined as an unexpected phenotypic outcome observed upon simultaneous perturbations (or knock-outs) of two genes that cannot be explained from the genes' individual effects (Beltrao et al., 2010; Fisher, 1930; Mani et al., 2008).
evidence: This definition is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Genetic interactions can be discovered using pairwise perturbations of genes, a strategy which has been experimentally used at large scale in yeast, C. elegans, Drosophila, E. coli and human cells.
source: Genetic interactions can be discovered using pairwise perturbations of genes, a strategy which has been experimentally used at large scale in yeast (Collins et al., 2007; Costanzo et al., 2010; Fiedler et al., 2009; Tong et al., 2001), C. elegans (Lehner et al., 2006), Drosophila (Fischer et al., 2015; Horn et al., 2011), E. coli (Babu et al., 2011) and human cells (Kampmann et al., 2013; Laufer et al., 2013; Roguev et al., 2013; Shen et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous work in different model organisms.

claim: Genes involved in the same cellular processes have highly similar genetic interaction profiles.
source: Several studies have shown that genes involved in the same cellular processes have highly similar genetic interaction profiles, which therefore can be used to create maps of cellular processes at a genome-wide scale (Costanzo et al., 2010; Costanzo et al., 2016; Fischer et al., 2015; Pan et al., 2018; Rauscher et al., 2018; Tsherniak et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017; Yu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a general principle supported by multiple cited studies.

claim: Multivariate phenotypes allow inferring the direction of specific genetic interactions and predicting a hierarchy of epistatic relationships of components in genetic networks.
source: Importantly, by allowing to infer the direction of specific genetic interactions, multivariate phenotypes further opened the possibility to predict a hierarchy of epistatic relationships of components in genetic networks (Fischer et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Most studies of genetic interactions focused on 'static' environmental conditions, ignoring the impact of context-dependent changes.
source: To date, most studies of genetic interactions focused on 'static' environmental conditions (e.g. under optimal culture conditions), ignoring the impact of context-dependent changes.
evidence: This is an assessment of the state of the field based on the authors' knowledge.

claim: Several studies have analyzed the influence of environmental changes on genetic interactions.
source: Recently, several studies have more specifically analyzed the influence of environmental changes on genetic interactions (Bandyopadhyay et al., 2010; Billmann and Boutros, 2017; Díaz-Mejía et al., 2018; Guénolé et al., 2013; Martin et al., 2015; St Onge et al., 2007; Wong et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Bandyopadhyay et al. (2010) defined static, positive and negative differential interactions that vary under changing environmental conditions.
source: For example, Bandyopadhyay et al. (2010) defined static, positive and negative differential interactions that vary under changing environmental conditions.
evidence: This is a specific finding from a cited study.

claim: Widespread changes in genetic interactions occur upon changes in environmental conditions.
source: These studies demonstrated that widespread changes in genetic interactions occur upon changes in environmental conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple cited studies.

claim: RNA interference (RNAi) can be used to perturb gene function with high efficiency and specificity to study gene function and map genetic interactions in Drosophila tissue cell culture.
source: RNA interference (RNAi) can be used to perturb gene function with high efficiency and specificity to study gene function and map genetic interactions in Drosophila tissue cell culture (Heigwer et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Little is known about the trajectories genetic interaction networks 'rewire' over time.
source: To date, little is known about the trajectories genetic interaction networks 'rewire' over time and models for their analysis as well as proof-of-principle data sets are missing.
evidence: This identifies a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Ras signaling is an important oncogenic pathway and Ras and EGFR family proteins are frequently mutated in cancer.
source: Ras signaling is an important oncogenic pathway and Ras and EGFR family proteins are frequently mutated in cancer (Rodriguez-Viciana et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: MEK1/2 acts downstream of Ras and phosphorylates ERK1/2.
source: MEK1/2 (the ortholog of Drosophila Dsor1) acts downstream of Ras and phosphorylates ERK1/2 (the ortholog of Drosophila rl), which phosphorylates many other proteins (e.g. ETS-family transcription factors [Friedman et al., 2011]).
evidence: This describes a known signaling pathway relationship supported by a citation.

claim: The topology of the Ras signaling pathway and its key components are widely conserved between human and Drosophila.
source: The topology of the Ras signaling pathway and its key components are widely conserved between human and Drosophila (Kolch, 2005; Perrimon, 1994; Wassarman et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In Drosophila, the Ras-pathway has been implicated in early embryonic patterning, growth of wing imaginal discs, differentiation of photoreceptors and blood cell proliferation.
source: In Drosophila, the Ras-pathway has been implicated in early embryonic patterning, growth of wing imaginal discs, differentiation of photoreceptors and blood cell proliferation (Asha et al., 2003; Prober and Edgar, 2000; Wassarman et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The study performed a series of high-throughput image-based genome-wide RNAi screens to identify a set of 168 genes with phenotypic profiles sensitive to MEK inhibition.
source: In this study, we first performed a series of high-throughput image-based genome-wide RNAi screens to identify a set of 168 genes with phenotypic profiles sensitive to MEK inhibition.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach and results.

claim: The study created a 168 × 76 double-perturbation matrix and measured the effect of 12,768 gene-gene perturbations under differential time and treatment conditions.
source: To construct the differential genetic interaction network, we then created a 168 × 76 double-perturbation matrix and measured the effect of 12,768 gene-gene perturbations under differential time and treatment conditions.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The perturbations were characterized by 16 reproducible and non-redundant phenotypic features.
source: These perturbations were characterized by 16 reproducible and non-redundant phenotypic features.
evidence: This describes the phenotypic measurements used in the study.

claim: Context-dependent interactions mapped the plasticity of Ras signaling and cross-talk to other signaling pathways, such as Rel and Stat signaling.
source: Context-dependent interactions mapped the plasticity of Ras signaling and cross-talk to other signaling pathways, such as Rel and Stat signaling.
evidence: This is a key finding from the study.

claim: The formation of measurable genetic interactions appears to be time dependent.
source: Based on the observation that the formation of measurable genetic interactions appears to be time dependent (Figure 1A), our study aims to extend the previously established framework of differential genetic interactions by adding a time component.
evidence: This observation is supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Different interactions-scores (π) are found at different time points when genetic interactions are quantified.
source: Often, when genetic interactions such as a synthetic sick or lethal interaction between two genes are quantified, different interactions-scores (π) are found at different time points (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Time influences the experimental outcome of genetic interaction measurements systematically.
source: This indicates that, next to a perturbation by external stresses (e.g. chemicals), also time influences the experimental outcome of genetic interaction measurements systematically.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of time-dependent interaction scores.

claim: The study used a cell morphology assay and automated image analysis in Drosophila cells to recover a broad spectrum of cellular phenotypes upon MEK-inhibition.
source: To recover a broad spectrum of cellular phenotypes upon MEK-inhibition, we used a cell morphology assay and automated image analysis in Drosophila cells (Breinig et al., 2015; Fischer et al., 2015; Horn et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used, supported by citations.

claim: Willoughby et al. (2013) showed that multiple small molecule MEK inhibitors significantly reduced the levels of phosphorylated rl in S2 cell culture.
source: Willoughby et al. (2013) previously compared the effect of multiple small molecule MEK inhibitors in vivo and in S2 cell culture and showed that all but one inhibitor significantly reduced the levels of phosphorylated rl.
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: The study used automated high-throughput microscopy combined with a real-time image analysis framework to record morphological phenotypes on a single-cell level.
source: Using automated high-throughput microscopy combined with a real-time image analysis framework we then recorded morphological phenotypes on a single-cell level.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: Genes involved in gene-gene interactions are enriched for genes that themselves display a phenotype distinguishable from the wild type.
source: Previous studies have found that genes involved in gene-gene interactions are enriched for genes that themselves display a phenotype distinguishable from the wild type (Deshpande et al., 2017; Koch et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The study performed multiple genome-wide RNAi screens under different environmental conditions.
source: To this end, we performed multiple genome-wide RNAi screens under different environmental conditions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Materials and methods, Appendix 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach.

claim: The study selected 168 genes for gene-gene interaction analysis based on specific criteria including high reproducibility, high correlation between dsRNA reagents, measurable effects, differential phenotypes upon Dsor1 inhibition, and expression in S2 cells.
source: For the following gene-gene interaction analysis, we selected a set of 168 genes from the genome-wide screens that showed: (i) high reproducibility between biological replicates, (ii) high correlation between sequence-independent dsRNA reagents (Pearson's correlation coefficient [PCC]> 0.5), (iii) measurable effects that deviate from the negative controls, (iv) differential phenotypes upon Dsor1 inhibition, and (v) are expressed in S2 cells (log normalized read count > 0, see Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the gene selection criteria used in the study.

claim: The 168 target genes include genes involved in Ras signaling, innate immunity, Wnt signaling, mRNA splicing, protein translation, cell cycle regulation, Jak/STAT and Tor signaling.
source: The resulting gene list for gene-gene interaction screening includes 168 target genes that also cover a number of signaling pathways including Ras signaling, innate immunity, Wnt signaling, mRNA splicing, protein translation, cell cycle regulation, Jak/STAT and Tor signaling (see Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This describes the functional categories of genes selected for the study.

claim: The query gene set contained 76 well-described genes to aid biological interpretability.
source: The query gene set, a subset of the 168 target genes, contained 76 well-described genes to aid biological interpretability.
evidence: This describes the composition of the query gene set.

claim: The combinatorial gene-gene matrix covering 168 target genes and 76 query genes was used to measure 12768 genetic interactions under different conditions.
source: A combinatorial gene-gene matrix covering 168 target genes and 76 query genes was used to measure 12768 genetic interactions under the different conditions.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The library was screened under MEK (Dsor1) inhibitor and control conditions at 48, 72 and 96 hr after compound addition.
source: The library was screened under MEK (Dsor1) inhibitor and control conditions at 48, 72 and 96 hr after compound addition.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: The screen was performed using two sequence-independent dsRNA design replicates and in two biological replicates for each condition.
source: The screen was performed using two sequence-independent dsRNA design replicates and in two biological replicates for each condition.
evidence: This describes the experimental replication strategy.

claim: In total 4.4 Mio. fluorescent images were captured, and 155 image features measured the perturbation effects for every single cell in the experiment.
source: In total 4.4 Mio. fluorescent images were captured, and 155 image features measured the perturbation effects for every single cell in the experiment (Appendix 1).
evidence: This quantifies the scale of the imaging data collected.

claim: Less than 3% of all plates were excluded according to quality control criteria.
source: Overall,<3% of all plates were excluded according to these criteria.
evidence: This describes the quality control results.

claim: Most of the 155 features showed a high reproducibility (80% having a PCC greater than 0.6).
source: Most of the 155 features showed a high reproducibility (80% having a PCC greater than 0.6, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This describes the reproducibility of the phenotypic features, supported by data in a figure supplement.

claim: Cell count and actin eccentricity were among the features with the highest replicate correlation.
source: The two features cell count (relative cellular fitness) and actin eccentricity (morphology of cells) were among the features with the highest replicate correlation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B)
evidence: This is supported by data shown in figure supplements.

claim: 90% of sequence-independent dsRNA pairs correlate with a PCC >0.6 with an average correlation of PCC = 0.77.
source: In addition, 90% of sequence-independent dsRNA pairs correlate with a PCC >0.6 with an average correlation of PCC = 0.77 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This describes the correlation between independent dsRNA designs, supported by data in a figure supplement.

claim: 16 features were selected for further analysis after reducing overlap by clustering features according to pairwise PCC of genetic interactions.
source: Since many of the remaining 114 features provide redundant information (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), overlap was reduced by first clustering all features according to the pairwise PCC of the genetic interactions. Second, we fixed the first feature (cell number) and removed all remaining features that correlated with PCC >0.7. Third, we selected the next most reproducible and biologically interpretable feature and removed all highly correlated features; this scheme was iterated until all features were passed. The remaining 16 features (see Supplementary file 3) were selected for further analysis.
evidence: This describes the feature selection process.

claim: Cell number and actin eccentricity show a weak correlation (PCC = 0.48) and thus provide independent information.
source: As a confirmation, we verified that cell number and actin eccentricity show a weak correlation (PCC = 0.48) and thus provide independent information (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a verification of the feature selection approach, supported by data in a figure supplement.

claim: The multivariate Z'-factor between RasGAP1 and Pvr was 0.814, indicating high assay quality.
source: An analysis of the multivariate Z'-factors between RasGAP1, a negative regulator of Ras signaling and Pvr, a positive regulator of Ras signaling (Zhang et al., 1999) showed a multi-variate Z' of 0.814, indicating high assay quality (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This describes the assay quality metric, supported by data in a figure supplement and a citation.

claim: There is significant agreement between π-scores measured in various features in this study and previous studies of genetic interactions in Drosophila S2 cell culture.
source: To this end, we compared gene-gene interactions that overlapped between this and previous studies of genetic interactions in Drosophila S2 cell culture (Figure 2—figure supplement 4). We found significant agreement between π-scores measured in various features in the different studies (FDR << 0.1, for linear dependence between π-scores measured in different studies).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous studies, supported by data in a figure supplement.

claim: There is high correlation of interactions between biological replicates for the phenotypic features 'DNA eccentricity' and 'cell number'.
source: Next, we confirmed a high correlation of interactions between biological replicates, as illustrated on the phenotypic features 'DNA eccentricity' and 'cell number' (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 5A,A').
evidence: This describes the reproducibility of the interaction measurements, supported by data in figures.

claim: Target and query RNAi reagents produce highly correlated interaction phenotypes regardless of assignment (PCC = 0.76 for cell number; PCC = 0.75 for actin eccentricity).
source: Our analysis demonstrated that both combinatorial conditions highly correlate (Figure 2—figure supplement 5B,B', PCC = 0.76 for cell number; PCC = 0.75 for actin eccentricity).
evidence: This demonstrates the symmetry of genetic interactions, supported by data in figure supplements.

claim: Different features provide independent information about genetic interactions as indicated by low correlation (PCC = −0.21 and 0.04).
source: We furthermore confirmed that different features provide independent information about genetic interactions as indicated by low correlation (PCC = −0.21 and 0.04, Figure 2—figure supplement 5C,C').
evidence: This confirms the independence of different phenotypic features, supported by data in figure supplements.

claim: S2 cells show a sustained phenotypic response toward PD-0325901.
source: These experiments demonstrated that S2 cells show a sustained phenotypic response toward PD-0325901.
evidence: This is a conclusion from dose-response experiments.

claim: There is high correlation (PCC = 0.81) between small molecule and RNAi perturbation of MEK, indicating high compound specificity.
source: A high correlation (PCC = 0.81) between small molecule and RNAi perturbation of MEK indicates high compound specificity.
evidence: This demonstrates the specificity of the MEK inhibitor used.

claim: The most drastic phenotypic changes among a number of features occurred in a concentration window around the drug's ED50 (1.5 nM).
source: The most drastic phenotypic changes among a number of features occurred in a concentration window around the drug's ED50 (1.5 nM).
evidence: This describes the dose-response relationship.

claim: A concentration of 1.5 nM PD-0325901 was selected as an optimal condition for the co-RNAi screening experiments.
source: Thus, we selected a concentration of 1.5 nM PD-0325901 as an optimal condition for the co-RNAi screening experiments.
evidence: This describes the experimental design decision based on dose-response data.

claim: The knockdown phenotypes of known Ras pathway components Dsor1 and drk showed a high correlation (PCC = 0.91).
source: We also found that the knockdown phenotypes of known Ras pathway components Dsor1 (MEK1/2) and drk showed a high correlation (PCC = 0.91, Figure 2—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This demonstrates that functionally related genes have similar phenotypes, supported by data in a figure supplement.

claim: Knockdown phenotypes of genes with antagonizing function like RasGAP1 and Dsor1 inversely correlate (PCC = −0.78).
source: Accordingly, knockdown phenotypes of genes with antagonizing function like the negative regulator of Ras signaling RasGAP1 and Dsor1 inversely correlate (PCC = −0.78).
evidence: This demonstrates that genes with opposing functions have opposite phenotypes.

claim: dsRNA targeting the same gene were highly reproducible producing similar phenotypic vectors (e.g. PCCRasGAP1 = 0.88).
source: dsRNA targeting the same gene were also highly reproducibly producing similar phenotypic vectors (e.g. PCCRasGAP1 = 0.88).
evidence: This demonstrates the reproducibility of RNAi reagents.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of phenotypic profiles recapitulated known functional relationships of Ras pathway components.
source: Hierarchical clustering of phenotypic profiles recapitulated known functional relationships of Ras pathway components, whereas regulators of translation show distinct phenotypes.
evidence: This demonstrates that the phenotypic assay captures biologically meaningful relationships.

claim: Over 1.3 million gene-gene interactions were analyzed in two conditions, three time points and 16 cellular features.
source: Overall, we analyzed over 1.3 million gene-gene interactions in two conditions, three time points and 16 cellular features.
evidence: This quantifies the scale of the interaction analysis.

claim: 72922 interactions showed a significant deviation from the expected combinatorial phenotype.
source: 72922 interactions showed a significant deviation from the expected combinatorial phenotype.
evidence: This quantifies the number of significant genetic interactions detected.

claim: Only 9090 (12%) genetic interactions are measured significantly (moderated t-test [limma], FDR < 0.1) for the cell number phenotype.
source: Only 9090 (12%) genetic interactions are measured significantly (moderated t-test [limma], FDR < 0.1) for the cell number phenotype underlining the value of the multiparametric analysis.
evidence: This demonstrates the advantage of using multiple phenotypic features.

claim: The analyses recapitulated known genetic interactions, such as negative interactions between Ras signaling components and the Jak/STAT pathway.
source: We found that our analyses recapitulated known genetic interactions. For example, Ras signaling components showed negative interactions with the Jak/STAT pathway (e.g. Pvr, dos and Sos show negative genetic interactions with dome and Stat92E (STAT5B), Baeg et al., 2005; Li et al., 2003; Xu et al., 2011).
evidence: This validates the approach by showing it recovers known interactions, supported by citations.

claim: The observed interactions become stronger over the three time points measured.
source: The observed interactions become stronger over the three time points measured, and interactions such as a negative interaction between Ras signaling components and Rho1 are stronger upon MEK inhibitor treatment.
evidence: This describes the time-dependent behavior of genetic interactions.

claim: A robust linear model of serial measurements (MODIFI) identifies the most differential interactions (4723 in total, 2.31% of all possible interactions, FDR < 0.1).
source: We found that a robust linear model of serial measurements (MODIFI, Figure 3A) identifies the most differential interactions (4723 in total, 2.31% of all possible interactions, FDR < 0.1).
evidence: This demonstrates the performance of the MODIFI method.

claim: MODIFI increased statistical power, identifying 147% more differential interactions across all features when compared to the best endpoint measurements (4723 vs 1907; 96 hr/rlm).
source: We further found that MODIFI increased statistical power, identifying 147% more differential interactions across all features when compared to the best endpoint measurements (4723 vs 1907; 96 hr/rlm).
evidence: This quantifies the improvement in sensitivity of the MODIFI method.

claim: By employing robust statistics MODIFI outperforms conventional models and more accurately estimates the parameters treatment sensitivity δ and the time dependence σ.
source: We conclude that by employing robust statistics MODIFI outperforms conventional models and more accurately estimates the parameters treatment sensitivity δ and the time dependence σ.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the performance of MODIFI based on the data.

claim: The unweighted residuals of each fit compared with the actual experimental variance measured at each time point show that remaining residuals of fit are explained by the variance between biological replicates (avg. PCC = 0.96, R2 = 0.92).
source: Analyses of all interactions for each phenotypic feature reveals that this is rarely the case (Figure 3—figure supplement 1). In most models, remaining residuals of fit are explained by the variance between biological replicates (avg. PCC = 0.96, R2 = 0.92).
evidence: This validates the linear model approach, supported by data in a figure supplement.

claim: The π-score dependence on time and treatment for each phenotypic feature can be reliably quantified using linear model statistics.
source: We thus concluded that the π-score dependence on time and treatment for each phenotypic feature can be reliably quantified using linear model statistics.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the model validation analysis.

claim: Treatment-sensitive interactions were equally likely to be positively or negatively shifted over all analyzed genes.
source: We found that treatment-sensitive interactions were equally likely to be positively or negatively shifted over all analyzed genes (Figure 3C, grey distribution).
evidence: This describes the overall distribution of treatment effects, supported by data in a figure.

claim: Treatment-sensitive interactions of Rel or Ras/Map and Jak/STAT related genes enriched as either negatively shifted π-score or positively shifted π-scores because of MEK inhibition, respectively.
source: Of note, especially treatment-sensitive interactions of Rel (NFKB1, a downstream effector of the Drosophila Imd signaling pathway, Myllymäki et al., 2014), or Ras/Map and Jak/STAT related genes enriched as either negatively shifted π-score or positively shifted π-scores because of MEK inhibition, respectively.
evidence: This describes pathway-specific patterns of treatment sensitivity, supported by a citation.

claim: Pathways which are positively regulated by MEK tend to form interactions that are less aggravating under MEK inhibition.
source: This implies that pathways which are positively regulated by MEK tend to form interactions that are less aggravating under MEK inhibition.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed pattern of treatment sensitivity.

claim: Interactions formed by Rel are negatively enhanced by MEK inhibition.
source: Interactions formed by Rel are negatively enhanced by MEK inhibition.
evidence: This describes a specific finding about Rel interactions.

claim: There is no or little significant difference between housekeeping modules (such as proteasome, translation machinery) and all genes in treatment sensitivity (p>0.1, two-sided KS-test).
source: We further found no or little significant difference between housekeeping modules (such as proteasome, translation machinery) and all genes (p>0.1, two-sided KS-test).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of treatment sensitivity across different gene categories.

claim: Components of the same pathway share differential interaction sensitivity and directionality in response to Ras pathway inhibition.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that components of the same pathway share differential interaction sensitivity and directionality in response to Ras pathway inhibition.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of treatment sensitivity patterns.

claim: MODIFI identified four main types of time and treatment-dependent interactions.
source: Assessing all interactions for which MODIFI identified statistically significant hits (FDR < 0.1), we identified four main types of time and treatment-dependent interactions that we expected would be recovered by MODIFI (Materials and methods, Figure 1C III-VI).
evidence: This describes the classification of interactions based on MODIFI results.

claim: Prosbeta4 and mts show an alleviating treatment-insensitive interaction that strengthens over time.
source: This is for example the case for mts knockdown (PP2CA, lethal by itself; Snaith et al., 1996) where the simultaneous loss of the proteasomal subunit Prosbeta4 (PSMB2, Wójcik and DeMartino, 2002) dominates the combinatorial phenotype that do not change further regardless of the treatment. In this case, a positive interaction that strengthens over time was measured (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a specific example of an interaction type, supported by data in a figure and citations.

claim: ksr and rl show an aggravating treatment-insensitive interaction.
source: For example, ksr (KSR1) and rl (ERK1/2), two core members of the Ras signaling cascade (Morrison, 2001; Wassarman et al., 1995), interact significantly (p=0.0017). This synthetic sick interaction is stable upon MEK inhibition and thus appears independent of phospho-rl levels which hints toward a kinase-independent function of rl in combination with its scaffolding protein ksr (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a specific example of an interaction type, supported by data in a figure and citations.

claim: skd and Stat92E show a positive treatment-sensitive interaction where MEK inhibition lifts the synthetic lethal phenotype.
source: For instance, skd (MED13, an integral component of the mediator complex; Janody et al., 2003) showed a positive differential interaction with Stat92E (Drosophila ortholog of human STAT receptor; Bina and Zeidler, 2009) (Figure 4C). Under control conditions skd knockdown aggravated the fitness loss induced by Stat92E knockdown to a lethal phenotype. This aggravation was attenuated under MEK inhibition.
evidence: This is a specific example of an interaction type, supported by data in a figure and citations.

claim: Rel and pnt show a negative treatment-sensitive interaction where Rel knockdown rescued the pnt knockdown phenotype under normal conditions but aggravated it after MEK inhibition.
source: In contrast, a negative differential interaction occurred between Rel and pnt. While Rel knockdown rescued the fitness-defect induced by pnt knockdown under normal conditions, it aggravated the pnt knockdown phenotype after MEK inhibition (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a specific example of an interaction type, supported by data in a figure.

claim: The aggravating interaction between skd and Stat92E and the alleviating interaction of Rel and pnt depend on the proper function of Dsor1.
source: Thus, we hypothesize that both, the aggravating interaction between skd and Stat92E and the alleviating interaction of Rel and pnt depend on the proper function of Dsor1.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed treatment-sensitive interactions.

claim: There are considerably more treatment-insensitive than treatment-sensitive interactions for all features (18468 vs. 4723, 16 phenotypic features).
source: We found considerably more treatment-insensitive than treatment-sensitive interactions for all feature (18468 vs. 4723, 16 phenotypic features, Figure 4E).
evidence: This quantifies the relative abundance of different interaction types, supported by data in a figure.

claim: Specific phenotypic features capture surprisingly high numbers of alleviating (nuclear shape) or aggravating (nuclear texture) treatment-insensitive interactions.
source: While, as expected, the distribution of negative and positive interactions over all features was symmetric, specific phenotypic features capture surprisingly high numbers of alleviating (nuclear shape) or aggravating (nuclear texture) treatment-insensitive interactions.
evidence: This describes feature-specific patterns in interaction types.

claim: Different phenotypic features identify specific biological reactions of cells toward double gene perturbations.
source: This indicates that different phenotypic features identify specific biological reactions of cells toward double gene perturbations.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the feature-specific patterns observed.

claim: Core essential housekeeping genes show exceptionally high numbers of alleviating interactions on cell shape but simultaneously display mostly aggravated phenotypes on their nuclear texture.
source: Core essential housekeeping genes, for example, show exceptionally high numbers of alleviating interactions on cell shape but simultaneously display mostly aggravated phenotypes on their nuclear texture.
evidence: This describes a specific pattern for housekeeping genes.

claim: Treatment-sensitive interactions, compared to treatment-insensitive interactions, enriched in specific signaling pathways related to MEK inhibition.
source: Additionally, we found that treatment-sensitive interactions, compared to treatment-insensitive interactions, enriched in specific signaling pathways related to MEK inhibition.
evidence: This describes the pathway enrichment of treatment-sensitive interactions.

claim: Ribosome or spliceosome-related genes formed mostly alleviating and treatment-insensitive interactions.
source: While, for example, ribosome or spliceosome-related genes formed mostly alleviating and treatment-insensitive interactions (Figure 5A)
evidence: This describes the interaction pattern for specific gene categories, supported by data in a figure.

claim: The JNK pathway was enriched for alleviating treatment-insensitive and negative treatment-sensitive interactions.
source: the JNK pathway was enriched for alleviating treatment-insensitive and negative treatment-sensitive interactions (Figure 5B).
evidence: This describes the interaction pattern for the JNK pathway, supported by data in a figure.

claim: Ras signaling, Rel, Mediator signaling and Jak/STAT signaling were equally overrepresented in treatment-sensitive and treatment-insensitive interactions.
source: Other pathways, such as Ras signaling, Rel, Mediator signaling or Jak/STAT signaling were equally overrepresented in treatment-sensitive and treatment-insensitive interactions.
evidence: This describes the interaction pattern for specific pathways.

claim: The enrichment of treatment-insensitive interactions highlights pathways with large impact on the interaction network controlling cell viability.
source: Among the pathways tested, the enrichment of treatment-insensitive interactions highlights pathways with large impact on the interaction network controlling cell viability.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the enrichment patterns.

claim: The enrichment of differential interactions highlights mainly signaling pathways that are sensitive to MEK inhibition.
source: The enrichment of differential interactions highlights mainly signaling pathways that are sensitive to MEK inhibition.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the enrichment patterns.

claim: This study is the largest exploration of gene-gene-drug interactions based on multiparametric, non-essential phenotypes.
source: At this point, our study is the largest exploration of gene-gene-drug interactions based on multiparametric, non-essential phenotypes.
evidence: This is a claim about the scale and scope of the study.

claim: The study demonstrates how different vulnerabilities for a diverse set of automatically scored phenotypes change upon time and environmental conditions.
source: We demonstrate how different vulnerabilities for a diverse set of automatically scored phenotypes change upon time and environmental conditions.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's contributions.

claim: The modeling approach increases the confidence to call treatment sensitive interactions upon changes of environmental conditions.
source: Our modeling approach increases the confidence to call treatment sensitive interactions upon changes of environmental conditions.
evidence: This is a claim about the utility of the MODIFI method.

claim: The approach allows to map a correlation network of cellular modules that react coherently toward the external stimulus.
source: This allows to map a correlation network of cellular modules that react coherently toward the external stimulus.
evidence: This is a claim about the utility of the approach.

claim: When further studies of context-dependent genetic interactions become available, a comparative analysis will provide fundamental insights into how different cellular networks react to environmental stimuli with implications for therapy resistance and timing of drug treatments.
source: We expect that, when further studies of context-dependent genetic interactions will become available, a comparative analysis will provide fundamental insights into how different cellular networks react to environmental stimuli with implications for therapy resistance and timing of drug treatments.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.

claim: MODIFI could be further expanded to include terms assessing the influence of the treatment on the behavior over time (rate of interaction change).
source: In future studies, MODIFI could be further expanded to include terms assessing the influence of the treatment on the behavior over time (rate of interaction change).
evidence: This is a suggestion for future methodological development.

claim: This study introduced an experimental and analysis framework to explore time-dependent rewiring of genetic networks which can be used to dissect the complexity of biological networks in model organisms and human cells.
source: This study introduced an experimental and analysis framework to explore time-dependent rewiring of genetic networks which can be used to dissect the complexity of biological networks in model organisms and human cells.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's contributions.
